# Lada: the stories first, then the spelling

Before the spelling, the story. **Lada** earns its restoration the old way — through what was actually told.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**Origins.** Lada appears in slavic tradition as love, beauty, spring.  The name's meaning, "Lady, order", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

**Worship and Memory.** Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Lada in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

- **Meaning:** "Lady, order"

- **Pantheon:** Slavic

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Lada** stands at [/lada/](/lada/) — [lore](/lada/lore/), [scholars](/lada/scholars/), [patterns](/lada/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

## The Emblems

The name does not travel alone. **Name** — The restored form Lada, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.; **Domain** — Love, Beauty, Spring. Each emblem is filed in the temple's record with its own provenance, the same discipline the spelling gets.

## For the Voice

Say "lada" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Lada". The reconstructed line runs `/lada/` — the temple's pronunciation atlas carries the phonemes one by one.

The rules that govern it are not house style; they are the tradition's own scholarship, applied with the same care here as in any edition — and published, with the sources, so the file can be checked the way an edition can be checked. One decisive feature survives — a single, honest mark — which places the restoration in Tier-2: exact, and exactly labeled.

## The Record Behind the File

This restoration is not a styling choice. **Lada** is the form the Slavic scholarly record supports for the figure whose domain is Love, Beauty, Spring. The name itself carries the meaning "Lady, order". 

The canonical record draws on **Folklore (traditional oral narrative)** — General folklore; **Vyacheslav Ivanov & Vladimir Toporov, Studies in Slavic Antiquities** — Slavic mythology / structural reconstruction. Each mark in the restored spelling — every accent, length, and retained letter — is traceable to that record rather than to editorial preference.

The pattern atlas seats this restoration in 3 industries: **Beauty, Fashion & Cosmetics**, **Love, Dating & Relationships**, **Legal, Justice & Compliance**.

## Why the Restoration Holds

The ASCII fallback *lada* is useful only where Unicode cannot travel; it is not the name. *lada* loses the information the sources preserve, and a temple built on the fallback would be a temple built on a typo. The file stands where the sources stand: with **Lada**, restored and addressable at [/lada/](/lada/).
